Siddhiq vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 March, 2024
Author: Vivek Rusia
Bench: Vivek Rusia
 1
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Indore
 Cra No. 3172 of 2021
 (Siddhiq Vs The State Of Madhya Prades
 Dated : 15-03-2024
 Shri Trilok Chand Jain, learned counsel for the appe
 Shri Amit Rawal, learned Government Advocate for the
State.

entities.text:
High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Indore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Shri Anshul Rajpurohit, learned counsel for the complainant.

Vide order dated 18.07.2022, this Court has allowed the application for suspension of jail sentence
and grant of bail filed on behalf of the appellant who has been convicted for commission of offences
punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376(2)(n), 376(3) of the Indian Penal Code and Section 3/4 &
5(L)/6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 02.  Now the prosecutrix has filed an application i.e. I.A. No.13579/2022 seeking cancellation of aforesaid bail order on the ground that the present appellant tried to contact her by sending Whats App messages.

It is further submitted that FIR / Crime No.353/2022 under Section 354,
354(D)(1)(i), 354(ii) of the IPC & Sections 11(iv), 12 of the POCSO Act has been registered against him as from 01.09.2022 to 03.09.2022, he was staring her with bad intention near bus stand.

The prosecutrix has also filed the copy of show-cause notice issued under Section 8 of the Madhya Pradesh Rajya Suraksha Adhiniyam, 1990 in the FIR registered at Crime No.422/2023 under Sections 279, 337, 294, 323, 506, 34 of the IPC.
Thereafter, another document has been filed to show that vide order 07.11.2023 he has been externed for eight months under Section 5(A)(B) of the M.P. Rajya Suraksha Adhiniyam.

03. The appellant has filed reply to the aforesaid application by submitting that under Section 389(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 the Public Prosecutor has the only right to move an application for cancellation of the order of suspension of jail sentence.
He has not breached any conditions of the order of suspension.
The prosecutrix and her family members are looking for an opportunity to wreak vengeance against the appellant.
With external pressure, they got managed to register an FIR against him.
It is further submitted that he is already out of district and there is no threat to the prosecutrix.
In FIR No.353/2022, he has been granted benefit of anticipatory bail by this Court vide order dated 07.12.2022 passed in M.Cr.C. No.57619 of 2022.

His appeal under Siddhiq vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19963482/
1 Section 9 of the M.P. Rajya Suraksha Adhiniyam is pending before the Commissioner.

entities.text: Siddhiq vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 04. Shri T.C. Jain, learned counsel appearing for the appellant submits that this Court gave the benefit of suspension of jail sentence to the appellant by observing on merit that he was not given sufficient opportunity to examine the witnesses.
If he is sent to jail again, it would be in violation of his fundamental rights.
If the prosecutrix is aggrieved by the bail granted to the appellant in subsequent FIR, she may file an application for cancellation of bail.
05. Learned Government Advocate for the respondent / State submits that while investigating Crime No.353/2022, the police seized the mobile of the appellant and obtained CDR and tower locations.
As per the CDR and tower locations, at the time disclosed in the FIR, the appellant was near bus stand with the mobile phone.
The mobile number is registered in the name of brother of the appellant who is residing with him.
It is further submitted that Whats App chatting was recovered from the mobile of the present appellant.

He was trying to contact the prosecutrix from unknown number and she identified the appellant, immediately warned him not to contact her in future, therefore, prosecution supports the application for cancellation of the order suspending the jail sentence and the same be recalled.
06.

It is correct that the application for cancellation of bail is liable to be filed by the prosecution However, in the present case, the application is filed by the prosecutrix and the Government Advocate / Public Prosecutor is supporting the application and also made an oral prayer for cancellation of order suspending the jail sentence, therefore, objection taken by Shri Jain is rejected.

07. Shri T.C. Jain is right in contending that this Court granted the benefit of suspension of jail sentence looking to the merits of the case, but that time this Court gave prima facie opinion for suspending the jail sentence of the appellant and he was not given the clean chit.
The fact remains that appellant whose application under Section 389(1) of the Cr.P.C. was allowed and he was released on bail is supposed to maintain good conduct.

Certain conditions are already implied in the order of suspension that he would not commit any similar offence of which he is an accused and shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case.

08. In the present case, the appellant has been convicted under Section 376(2)(n) and sentenced to undergo 10 years' R.I., under Section 376, 20 years' R.I. and under Section 3/4 & 5(L)/6, 20 - 20 years' R.I. as the prosecutrix was minor at the time of commission of offence.
The appellant came up with a defence that she went along with him in hotel as they were in friendship.

She fully supported the case of prosecution and deposed against the appellant, her age was found below 16 years,
therefore, appellant should have made distance from her during bail period.
The investigation has revealed that the appellant tried to contact the prosecutirx by sending messages and staring her with bad intention for which the FIR was registered.
09. Looking to the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case, I.A. No.13579/2022 stands allowed.
The order giving the benefit of suspension of jail sentence dated 18.07.2022 is hereby recalled.
Bail bond stands discharged.
The appellant shall surrender before the police forthwith.
